label: input digit 2 at original positions 0-4
explanation: Token detector for the digit 2 as an input during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, limited to positions 0-4. It fires on every such step (precision 1.0) and on almost no others; it is silent for 2 at original positions 5+, on the delimiter, and on all other tokens. In the copy phase it fires only weakly and rarely, when 2 is fed back as an input at about step L+2. Magnitude depends on position: weakest at t=0 (about 0.18 of max), strongest at t=2-3. Top activations (max 1.77) are 2 at t=2 after the prefix 0 3. Within the profile, magnitude also rises with more digits earlier in the sequence (examples).

issues: Predicate reproduces on test: precision 1.000, recall 0.993, F1 0.996, mass recall 0.998, with 0 false positives.

The 599 missed steps on test (0.2% of mass) are all weak activations (0.04-0.29 of max) at step 5. These are input 2 at original position 5 or in the copy phase at recall_idx 2, which matches the explanation's 'rare copy-phase firing around L+2' caveat. Taken alone, those cases are not predictable: (phase==0)&(in_tok==2)&(t==5) has precision 0.023, and copy-phase in_tok==2 at recall_idx 2 has precision 0.020. So they are a small tail, not a gap that a better predicate could capture.

Minor: the claim that the 'activation rate goes up when the sequence has more digits' (n_digits 1/2/3 gives rate 0.015/0.026/0.034) is almost certainly a side effect of the predicate itself: more digits means more chances that a 2 lands at positions 0-4. It is not a separate property of the feature. The magnitude-by-history claim is already marked as unchecked.
Magnitude claims hold up: the t=0 share of mass (0.071) against t=2-3 (0.33/0.30) at similar counts fits a weak t=0 and a peak at t=2-3. The top examples are all '0 3 [2:1.00]'.
